title: Scaling law of variational quantum algorithms
abstract: We study scaling law of variational quantum algorithms by large-scale numerical experiments on combinatorial optimizations. On experiments up to n = 5000 qubits with O( log(n)) circuit depth with a classically simulable ansatz, the converged energies consistently differ by no more than 0.5% from the optimal or reference energies reported in the benchmarks.
summary: This work numerically studies the scalability of variational quantum algorithms for combinatorial optimization problems. By using a specialized matchgate ansatz and simulating up to 5000 qubits, the authors show that high accuracy can be maintained with only a logarithmic circuit depth. This validates the potential of VQAs for large-scale quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper investigates the scaling law of variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) when applied to solving complex combinatorial optimization problems.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that VQAs can maintain high convergence rates (exceeding 99.5%) to optimal energies on large-scale problems (up to 5000 qubits) using only a logarithmic circuit depth.
method: They employ a specialized, problem-independent matchgate ansatz and simulate the quantum state evolution using the covariance matrix representation, enabling efficient readout of multiple observables.
model_or_system: The model involves mapping combinatorial optimization problems (like QUBO or k-SAT) onto a diagonal Hamiltonian, which is then minimized using VQAs.
key_observables: Converged energy expectation values $\langle H_f angle_	heta$, and the approximation ratio relative to optimal/reference energies.
important_parameters: Number of qubits ($n$) up to 5000, and circuit depth scaling as $O(\log(n))$ for high accuracy.
main_assumptions: The efficiency relies on the matchgate ansatz allowing for polynomial-time classical simulation via Majorana covariance matrices, and the 'one state propagation, many observable readouts' technique.
figures_summary: FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 illustrate the scaling laws for k-SATs and QUBO, respectively, while FIG. 2 shows the structure of the matchgate ansatz circuit.
paper_structure: The paper is structured around presenting numerical experiments on various SAT/QUBO instances, detailing the efficient calculation of expectation values using Wick's theorem on the covariance matrix, and concluding with the demonstration of the observed scaling law.
why_interesting: The use of the matchgate ansatz, which is related to free evolution of 1+1D transversal Ising models, provides a concrete, hardware-implementable quantum circuit structure for benchmarking quantum algorithms.
